steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I've never tried to use the Black Crown to access your thoughts before, Doctor—

options: I've opened up my heart and mind for you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Thank you.
She looks to her side, at the beam of bright, warm light gently tugging at her hand.
She shuts her eyes, and slowly lets out a sigh of relief.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't know where this journey of ours will lead us, Doctor, but I'll protect you.
Under the watchful eye of Civilight Eterna, she gives your brow a light touch—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Your memories and emotions flow towards me.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...It's strange.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They billow so gently as they flow, and the memories' edge is close at hand...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What did Theresa see back then—
Amiya sees you, and Kal'tsit, and herself, and the many people aboard Rhodes Island.
As she walks deeper, the boundary of that one memory comes within reach. Curiosity and concern nearly cause her to forget her mission. She wants to reach out to touch it...
Touch upon the start of your memories. Chernobog, the Sarcophagus, and you, weakly stretching out your hand—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It looks like there's other memories too? Why are they so blurred?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Who was—
You grab ahold of Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I-I don't know. This is the first time I've ever dived so deep into someone else's mind. It's a very... odd feeling.

options: Good thing you pulled it off.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thankfully, yes. Now, I can sense even the faintest of your thoughts.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Aha, you sure are relaxed right now!

options: I've got nothing to worry about with you around.
So, what should we do next?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Hold my hand tight, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'll protect you on the road ahead. Theresa taught me everything about the role of King that day.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: 'She' awaits us, at the start of that path.

a.text: I get what you're saying, but I cannot provide what you're asking for, as your request violates the underlying logic of DWDB-221E.
But I do have a way to circumvent its limits, Kal'tsit—
Unfortunately, not even Theresa was able to penetrate this deeply. The risk was far beyond what she could bear—
You're not here for answers? Then why are you so insistent I access this data that is useless to you?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: 'I have no way of knowing if there will come a day that Amiya asks you the same question. But I hope that, in the darkness, she will find the way I lit for her.'

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: That was Kal'tsit's answer to me, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Could I ask you to look through all of Dr. Kal'tsit's access records for us?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I would be happy to.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Her every doubt, her every insistence, each and every time she left in disappointment. I will show it all to you, unreserved.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You have dove into the Civilight Eterna before, Amiya, but this time, what you seek lies far beyond your limits.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: It is a place where life on Terra cannot tread, for the time being, but perhaps you will find the chance to touch upon this knowledge that is not yours.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Because you have someone who walks alongside you. Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You will quickly understand what I mean, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Follow me, Amiya. Follow me to—
'Civilization's Singularity'.
A great hallway of pure white circles around a central point that defies comprehension. The Singularity.
An unending stream of complex information flows from it, but the strands you manage to snatch hold of are still within your understanding.
Amiya cannot see the way you entered, but after an interminably long time walking down the corridor, she finds herself back where she started.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You noticed, Amiya.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: The stagnation of civilization does not mean it stands still. It continues onwards on time's linear flow, unable to turn back.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: But all that life discovers and creates is doomed to fall into an inextricable cycle.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Mathematics, physics, philosophy, theology... These theories and practicalities, among others, cannot inspire hope as they once did.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: The ascending spiral has failed. Life squanders its future as it stumbles blindly in the dark.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So... this is as far as we can go?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Only as defined by Terra's current knowledge. It serves as a limit, yes, but it is also a safeguard.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: A safeguard?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Cognitive?

options: Like how we can't make sandbeasts calculate wave dynamics.
Even if we gave them all the data and formulae...
All forcing it will do is hurt their brains.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: As keen an intuition as ever, Doctor, but not entirely correct.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: DWDB-221E enlightens life at a steady pace to bring it forward. It does not simply reveal fragments of the future to the seeker to create evolutionary leaps that violate the laws of nature and ethics.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Knowledge cannot be unlearned, Amiya. The dreamers who glimpsed the true sky are no longer happy to slumber in ignorance on the ground.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Information beyond civilization's cognitive limits will simply blind them to reality, a deadly poison luring them into annihilation's embrace, throwing their civilization into the abyss.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: And so, this boundary was born.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But why does it... look so much like a prison made from some giant data server?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: It appears in a form your mind can comprehend, like how DWDB-221E appears as a black crown in the material world when accompanying you.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: To a minuscule ant, it is an ouroboric river, forever unable to flow to the sea.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: But to a celestial body whose lifespan stretch to the trillions, it is a gravitational field that will stay with them their entire life, unfathomable, inescapable.
You walk towards a section but one step away from the void. The distant singularity at the core calls to you.
Information washes past you like gentle waves, showing you glimpses of many fascinating sights.
They are fleeting shadows of your past, a life you have lost and forgotten.
Stray visions of an 'unfamiliar' era.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Be careful, Doctor!
Amiya tugs on your hand.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We don't know what will happen if you fall off this boundary—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are these... what you saw...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: —'The Originium slug egg' 'went through the bridge between stars'—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...So all those stories really did happen.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: When I was really, really young, I met someone who was incredibly caring.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That care was matched with a great weakness, but also a stubborn insistence in carrying me across a road laden with Originium shards.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: When I was dizzy with fever, yet too scared of nightmares to sleep, a patient voice regaled me with stories I had never heard before.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: In a dark and cramped cave, difficult-to-find ore samples were smashed without the slightest hesitation—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And the shining stones were scattered across the walls, and used to tell me tales of the stars, and the heavenly paradise above the clouds.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Would you like to hear one of those stories, Doctor?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There was once someone who drove a mysterious vehicle shaped like an Originium slug egg on their lonesome, who went through the bridge between stars.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: On the most quiet of nights, guides would borrow glowing clouds from old stars and make round mirrors out of them to light the way.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: On the other side of the bridge, spires faded in and out of the clouds, and the stars wore crowns of flowers.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: When descending on that crown, you'll see that it's a really, really big playground, one where lovely little children gather to play.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But it was hard for the vehicle's driver to stop...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The driver changed over to the most miraculous vehicle on hand, and drove it for many, many years...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But the years came to an end, and nobody was left.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Nobody but the driver.

options: Is the person in your story... me?

steps.text: Amiya grips your hand tightly.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thanks to my infection, it's hard for me to remember much from that time, and there's a lot from those stories I don't understand.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I will do everything I can to remember every single one of your stories.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Because they are my stories. Tales you told to me.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't want to forget them.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I never thought today would be the day I finally get to share your gift to me with you, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This time, we witnessed it together, you and I. We got to know this past life of yours once more.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Do you long for this kind of life, Doctor?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm not surprised. I'm very much the same. When I first thought of such wonders, I longed for it too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's the kind of life I could never truly have for myself.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I couldn't help myself from sharing them with Theresa, and the two of us would add many wondrous details of our own imagining—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Until it changed beyond recognition, flying ever further out of reach...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But now that I've had a glimpse with my own eyes, I don't think I'm that far away from your past life.

spans.text: But now that I've had a glimpse with my own eyes, I don't think I'm
far away from your past life.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Do you believe that one day, this great land will be just as beautiful, Dr. {@nickname}?

options: Perhaps it will be even more beautiful...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It will, and we'll be there to greet it.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Rhodes Island will be there to see the light of dawn.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You don't? Strange, it was such a beautiful life.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: One without the pain of Oripathy, without conflict or war, where children could live their lives in joy...

options: Maybe I didn't want to show you the crueler side of things.
There's always two sides to life, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Maybe you're right. The cruelty behind the happiness, the joy behind the suffering. We've experienced it all ourselves.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'll admit, I shared these wondrous stories with Theresa, and she was just as amazed as I was.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She always hoped that everyone in Kazdel... no, in all the lands would have the chance to experience such a life. She did her best to see it come true.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We can't let things slide back, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There may come a day that Rhodes Island will be able to see this beauty flourish across the land.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: 'Deep Dive'.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: The intact data stored within DWDB-221E is decoded by the singularity and exported in a moderated and suitable format as information.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: However, Amiya on her own will not be able to break through the limits of the baseline logic.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I am not certain, but the possibility is there.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But how are we supposed to get close to the information once it's exported?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Forgive me, Amiya, but I have no further information on this topic.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I will search through the clues Kal'tsit left behind, and sort anything that may be of use to you so that it is easier to find.

options: Perhaps we could build a bridge?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: A bridge?

options: Hasn't Kal'tsit already pointed the way for us?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Has anyone done something like that before?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: There is no precedent in the records.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...It's worth a try, either way.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Then you must be aware of the risks. The closer you get to the singularity, the denser the information will become. You may possibly experience it gaining mass.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Information with mass?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: It is possible here, yes.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: It is also possible that information not yet fully decoded will flood into your mind and destroy it.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: And a destroyed mind means...

steps.name: Voice From Within
steps.text: (Unknown language) Don't mind me, traveler. I'm simply watching yet another bout of destruction is all.

steps.name: Voice From Within
steps.text: (Unknown language) Hierda. That's your name, right?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Did you just say my name?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I don't know whatever language you're speaking in at all. Also, how'd you know—
As the Cautus passes by the porthole, she sees the figure out in the darkness of space slowly approach the ship, then disappear from her sights.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Who is that, Raydistorter?

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: (Fervent singing) ♪—♪—♪—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: —Is something wrong?!

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: There's not many of us who like her!

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Sorry, traveler, I simply can't handle being in the same room as her.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: If my friends saw this, they'd give me the cold shoulder because of it too.
When the bewildered Cautus snaps out of it, she finds herself the only person in the cabin. Upon foreseeing the arrival of an unwelcome soul, everyone else had made themselves scarce.
Then the Cautus sees her.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: No need to look so amazed. I learned how to communicate using long-distance resonance a while ago.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: At the very least, before destroying that odd race, I kept the unique language patterns they had evolved.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...D-Destroying?

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: (Sighs)

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: Do you detest destruction as well, our newly-come guest?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I... am not too sure what happened, to be honest.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: It's nothing too complicated. My people once ate stars to live. Others may hate us for it, but it's simply our survival instinct at work.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: But now, that past only exists in horror stories passed around the metaphorical campfire.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: My people are on the brink of extinction. I fear I may be the last of my kind, in fact.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: We destroy to live, but when true destruction finally bears down upon us, we are powerless in the face of it...

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: From that point onwards, I have become nothing more than a beggar. With the aid of some geniuses, I have changed the method I use to obtain the energy I need to live—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It sounds like... You've been trying to blend in with other lifeforms too.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: So when you were out in space looking at that dead planet, were you reminiscing about the destruction you experienced?

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: Reminiscing?

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: Haha, nothing of the sort.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: Everyone here has accepted the ruination chasing us with serenity and hope in their hearts.
